items.prompt: For n arriving values, what work does this frontier algorithm perform?

options.text: One O(log n) lower-bound search and O(1) append/replacement per value.
options.why: The frontier length is at most n, giving O(n log n) comparisons and O(n) stored values.

options.text: Enumerate all 2^n subsequences before choosing a tail.
options.why: The dominance frontier avoids enumerating witnesses.

options.text: Sort each whole prefix before every insertion.
options.why: bisect searches the already ordered frontier without sorting each prefix.

options.text: Use constant total memory because only the final tail matters.
options.why: The algorithm retains one tail per attainable length, potentially n entries.
